newsitem.title: UK: FTS&P indices to retain Hong Kong stocks post-1997.
newsitem.headline: FTS&P indices to retain Hong Kong stocks post-1997.

text.p: The FT/S&P Actuaries World Indices Committee is to retain the Hong Kong stockmarket within its world indices after the colony transfers to China in 1997.

"Following the transfer of Hong Kong to China in 1997, the current FT/S&P-Actuaries Hong Kong Index will be renamed 'Hong Kong, China'. Hong Kong and China will be treated as two separate regions within a single country," the committee said in a statement.
The indices are used by fund managers to allocate assets and measure performance.
The indices are compiled by FTSE International, Goldman Sachs and Standard and Poor's in conjunction with the Institute of Actuaries and the Faculty of Actuaries.
